subject: Private offer structuring — SKU bundling, commit earnbacks and distributor uplift
messages:
From: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@nimblehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@nimblehealth.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer: SKU packaging and distributor uplift questions

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The procurement team has run a first pass on the private offer you shared and we have a few open items before I can circulate to ops:

1) SKU bundling: Nimble wants to combine 'Large Inference' (L-1) and 'KV-cache' (K-1) into a single bundled SKU for the AWS private offer. Will that be treated as a single metered SKU or two linked SKUs for billing? We need the exact billing semantic because our marketplace connector maps to a single SKU per invoice line.

2) Commit earnbacks & overage: We need language for an earnback if committed usage is exceeded in the first 90 days. Any recommended thresholds for a commit ramp?

3) Distributor uplift: we work through a distributor (CloudBridge) and they expect a 12% uplift on list. Can that be modeled as an allowed channel margin so it passes through the private offer pricing, or do we need to create an explicit distributor rebate outside the PO?

I've attached our SKU mapping matrix to make this concrete. If easier, can we do a 30-minute call with you + legal + your deal ops?

Thanks —
Claire
Claire D'Souza
Head of Procurement, Nimble Health
Attachment: Nimble_SKU_requirements.xlsx
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: SKU packaging and distributor uplift questions

Claire —

Appreciate the clear matrix, that helps. Quick notes below; longer answers and a sample private-offer template attached.

1) SKU bundling: We can support both approaches. Pragmatic recommendation: publish a single bundled SKU in the PO that maps to an internal two-SKU accounting split. That keeps your marketplace connector simple (one invoice line) while letting us apply internal quotas (Large Inference + KV). If you need token-level attribution in reporting we can export a per-component breakdown in the monthly usage file.

2) Commit earnbacks & overage: Typical structure we use: a 3-month ramp with an earnback band of 80-110% (no earnback under 80%, pro-rata earnback between 80-100%, automatic overage billing above 110%). This balances predictable commit economics for you and avoids heavy retro credits for us. We can tighten/loosen based on your comfort.

3) Distributor uplift: Two options:
  - Allowable uplift in list price (simpler): we include a "reseller uplift" line in the PO metadata so the distributor invoice reflects the agreed % and the PO list is the channel-net price. This is easiest when distributor takes no additional margin layering.
  - Rebate outside PO (preferred if you need clear revenue recognition): we keep PO list price at net and run a separate distributor rebate (monthly) with supporting settlement files. This avoids confusing the PO amount vs. what Redwood books.

Which option you prefer depends on whether CloudBridge expects the uplift to be visible on the marketplace invoice or handled as a downstream settlement. If you want, I can loop Deal Ops (Irene) to sketch the accounting flow.

Suggested next steps:
- If you want the single bundled SKU approach, we'll send a draft PO file with the bundle and uplift metadata.
- If you prefer the separate rebate, we'll share the distributor settlement template and the monthly evidence file format.

I've attached our private-offer template and a short channel margin workback PDF to show both flows. Happy to jump on a call tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Marketplace Sales (North America)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: RDW-private-offer-template.xlsx, channel-margin-workback.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: SKU packaging and distributor uplift questions

Claire/Vanessa —

Quick finance note on distributor uplift: if Nimble wants CloudBridge to show a 12% uplift on the marketplace invoice, we need to confirm tax/pass-through treatment in both parties' accounting. Often easier to model as a rebate outside the PO so Redwood recognizes the same gross revenue and the distributor handles its uplift as a third-party settlement.

If you want, we can run a short three-line example (list, Redwood net, distributor uplift) so you can validate with CloudBridge accounting.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Deal Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@nimblehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@nimblehealth.com, CloudBridge Legal <legal@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: SKU packaging and distributor uplift questions

Vanessa / Ben —

Thanks for the clear options and the templates. Nimble's preference is:
- Single bundled SKU in the PO (simpler for our marketplace connector)
- Distributor uplift handled as a rebate/settlement outside the PO (CloudBridge wants the uplift visible to partners but our AR team prefers the PO to reflect Redwood net revenue)
- We'll accept the 3-month ramp with 80-110% earnback band as a starting point; legal will propose small wording tweaks.

Next steps for us:
1) I'll share your PO template with CloudBridge and internal AR this afternoon.
2) Please send the draft private offer with the bundle metadata and sample monthly usage export.
3) I'll create a short call invite for Monday 14 Mar 10:00am PT to finalize the settlement cadence.

Also sending a preliminary NDA for signature via DocuSign (link below) — that's just to allow CloudBridge to share their distributor fee schedule in the call.
